title: Kenyan Family Bean Stew
community: Enjoyed across all Kenyan communities at family gatherings
author: Mama Wanjiru
desc: Kenyan Family Bean Stew — the large-pot bean stew prepared for family gatherings and celebrations. Rich, thick, generously spiced, and made in quantities that feed the whole extended family. The essential side dish at every Kenyan celebration table.
longDesc: No Kenyan celebration is complete without a large pot of bean stew on the table — it is the dish that ensures everyone is fed, regardless of how many guests arrive, and it is the side that ties together the meat and rice dishes of the feast. Prepared at scale with more spice and more care than the everyday version, family bean stew is deeply satisfying and universally beloved.
ingredients: 800g dried mixed beans — red kidney, borlotti, and black-eyed peas
steps: Cook in fresh water for 60—75 minutes until tender. Drain, reserve 2 cups liquid.
Heat oil in large pot. Cook onions until deeply golden — 10 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomatoes, tomato paste, and spices. Cook for 10 minutes until very thick.
Add cooked beans and reserved liquid.
Simmer for 20—25 minutes until thick and richly flavoured.
Season generously. Garnish with fresh coriander.
chefTips: Mixed beans are better than single variety for celebration — more colour, flavour, and texture variation.
Prepare a day ahead — bean stew always tastes better the next day.
Cook a larger quantity than you think you need — it always runs out first.
commonMistakes: Under-seasoning at scale — taste and adjust generously.
Not cooking the beans fully before the sauce stage.
cookingScience: Bean stew improves significantly when reheated — the overnight resting allows the spices to continue to permeate the beans and the sauce to thicken further as more starch leaches from the beans into the liquid.
sustainabilityTips: Bean stew is the most sustainable protein dish at any celebration.
Beans are nitrogen-fixing — the most environmentally responsible protein source.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 5 days. Freeze for 3 months.
reheating: Reheat gently on stovetop — improves with reheating.
healthBenefits: Rich in iron, folate, and potassium.
culturalNote: Family bean stew is the great equaliser of the Kenyan celebration table — it ensures that every guest, whether they eat meat or not, has a rich, satisfying, deeply flavourful dish. No celebration is properly catered without it.
